To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mutant of Escherichia colt that grows at 42 degrees C in the presence, but not in the absence, of added tRNA is deficient in the activity of elongation factor T (EF-T) and that EF-T is an essential component of the protein-synthetic machinery.
(1) the mutant has a temperature-sensitive elongation factor Ts, (2) the mutant has no detectable elongation factor Ts at 42°.
EF-Ts is an essential protein that is involved in the elongation of the polypeptide chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the function of the EFs in the translation process.

the following questions: 1. What are the properties of EF-Ts? 2. What is the function of EF-Ts in tRNA? 3. Is the EF-Ts mutant altered in its interaction with tRNA? 4. What are the consequences of EF-Ts deficiency on the cell?
the following questions: (1) How is the tRNA molecule recognized by EF Ts, the EF responsible for binding of the aminoacyl-tRNA to the ribosome?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this class of mutant is defective in a factor required for tRNA charging, but that the lesion is in EF-Ts.
the EF-Ts mutant is defective in the binding of EF-Ts to the ribosome and that this defect is due to a lesion in EF-Ts itself.
the mutant is a conditional mutant in the EF-Ts gene, and that this gene is essential for growth at 30° C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tRNAs and EF Ts are functionally interdependent.
the EF Ts mutant, like the tRNA mutant, requires tRNA for growth at 42° but that, unlike the tRNA mutant which is temperature-sensitive for growth at 37°, it is not temperature-sensitive for growth.
the EF-Ts of the mutant is altered in a way that makes it unable to function at 30° C, but that it can be activated by tRNA at 42°.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tRNA is a key element in the regulation of gene expression in the cell.
the tRNA and the EF are both required to grow at 42°.
the mutant EF-Ts is defective in its binding of aminoacyl-tRNA.
